title: It’s thinking
lede: The launch campaign as it aired, local news from launch night, the wire footage of the day Sega quit, and a later look back.

videos.title: “Apocalypse,” the 9/9/99 launch commercial
videos.caption: The big-budget spot by Foote, Cone & Belding, filmed in Vancouver. Peter Moore says it ran once, on launch night during the MTV Video Music Awards.[^6] This copy is a fan restoration uploaded in 2025.

videos.title: The “It’s Thinking” commercials, 1999–2000
videos.caption: A six-minute reel of the short spots that introduced the console in the United States. The years are the uploader’s.

videos.title: KATU News: the Dreamcast launch
videos.caption: Local television coverage from Portland, Oregon. The station says it originally aired on September 9, 1999.

videos.title: SegaNet commercial
videos.caption: A spot for Sega’s online service. The uploader dates it 1999; SegaNet opened on September 7, 2000,[^14] so we list it under 2000.

videos.title: AP: “Japan: Sega announces future of Dreamcast”
videos.caption: Associated Press footage of the Tokyo news conference on January 31, 2001, where vice president Hideki Sato announced the end of production.[^4]

videos.title: IGN: “The Rise and Fall of the Sega Dreamcast”
videos.caption: A five-minute retrospective published in 2015. Its figures are IGN’s; ours are in the sections above.
